name: Cart Conversion Boost
author: cartconversionboost

sections.description:
Cart Conversion Boost helps you increase your checkout conversion rate by first helping you take the name and email before the shopping cart (so you can follow up with the cart abandonment to bring back sales), and then passing the customer’s name and email from your opt-in form into your ThriveCart checkout page *. It works with:

  • Thrive Themes opt-in forms (Thrive Architect and Thrive Leads, including 2-step lightbox opt-ins)
  • Kit (formerly ConvertKit) forms on your WordPress site (Kit’s embedded forms, the Kit plugin’s Form block, and the Kit plugin’s Form Builder block)
  • Elementor Pro forms and popups
  • Any other opt-in form or page builder – Flodesk, BirdSend, MailerLite, Mailchimp, ActiveCampaign, AWeber, GetResponse, Brevo, HubSpot, Contact Form 7, WPForms, Fluent Forms, Gravity Forms, Divi, Beaver Builder, Bricks and hand-written HTML forms – as long as the form sits on your page (not inside an iframe) and sends people to your Cart Conversion Boost URL
  • “Buy” Button Pop-up (new) – no pop-up builder? Cart Conversion Boost has its own. Tick/check it on, paste your email tool’s opt-in form (Flodesk, BirdSend, MailerLite, ActiveCampaign, AWeber, GetResponse, EmailOctopus, Mailchimp, Brevo, a form plugin and others) and link any Buy button to #ccb-popup-1, or use the shortcode [ccb_buy_button popup="1" text="Buy Now"]. Visitors sign up in the pop-up and land on your pre-filled checkout; visitors you already know skip it (Silent opt-in, popup is never seen, but they do go into your cart-abandonment list). Ready-made “Order step” look with an editable headline, step cue and progress bar

Take the customer details before they get to the shopping cart, so you can follow up, and convert more to completed sale, in case of cart abandonment.

When a visitor signs up through your pre-cart opt-in form (as the first part of their order), this plugin ensures their name and email address are automatically pre-filled on the ThriveCart payment page – reducing friction and improving the user experience.

The free version has every feature, for one product:

NOTE: “Known customer” means your site already took their name and email. That might be from a previous opt-in form or from them clicking a link with their name and email address in that link (often from an email you sent them). [We will show you how to set up this email link carrying their name and email, if you don’t already know.]

  • One product – one Cart Conversion Boost URL for one ThriveCart product. Its checkout can be on thrivecart.com, on your own checkout domain (for example pay.yourdomain.com), or embedded on one of your pages
  • Auto-fills your Buy links – on your pages, links to your product’s ThriveCart checkout or to your Cart Conversion Boost URL get the visitor’s details added automatically, so a 3-step funnel (opt-in, sales page, checkout) needs no special links
  • Sitewide Identity Persistence – For known customers, Sitewide Identity Persistence remembers the visitor across every page of your site for the rest of their visit, so the Buy button on any page opens a pre-filled checkout
  • Opt-in pre-fill – For known customers, pre-fill any of your opt-in forms with their name and email, so it’s one click to continue (GetResponse forms are the exception: GetResponse seals them off, so visitors type their details)
  • Silent opt-in – For known customers, when a visitor clicks a Buy button that would normally open a pop-up opt-in, the pop-up is not shown. Instead, its form is invisibly pre-filled in and submitted to your email system behind the scenes, so they still join your list for that form (for example your cart-abandonment list). They never see the popup and the next thing they see is the pre-filled checkout
  • Embedded and popup checkouts – your product’s ThriveCart checkout embedded on your own page is pre-filled too

Cart Conversion Boost Pro is the same plugin, but with unlimited products.

Disclaimer – Cart Conversion Boost is an independent plugin and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Thrive Themes, Kit or ThriveCart.

Video Overview

Watch how Cart Conversion Boost works in under 2 minutes:

Screenshots

  1. The plugin interface screenshot-1.jpg
  2. Paste your Cart Conversion Boost URL into your ThriveThemes optin form as the “Target URL”. Make sure to tick/check the “Send form values” field.
  3. Customer enters their name and email in the pre-sale opt-in
  4. Your ThriveCart checkout is automatically pre-filled with their name and email already, helping conversion to sale. No repeated typing.

🚀 Key Benefits

  • Improve conversion rates – more sales, same traffic
  • Reduced cart abandonment
  • Capture the lead before the payment page
  • Pre-fill ThriveCart checkout fields automatically
  • Reduce friction during checkout – Faster checkout experience
  • Simple setup inside WordPress admin
  • Lightweight and performance-friendly
  • NoCode interface

A smoother checkout experience often leads to higher completion rates and better user experience.

Why This Matters

Every extra step in a checkout process increases the chance that a customer abandons their purchase.

When customers must re-enter information they already provided, it introduces:

Friction
Delay
Drop-off risk

= Less sales.

Cart Conversion Boost removes this friction by connecting your opt-in form and your ThriveCart checkout.

🔗 How It Works

  1. A visitor completes your opt-in form (maybe from a squeeze or lead magnet page, or a pre-cart order pop-up), which captures their name and email and sends them to your email provider
  2. The Cart Conversion Boost plugin passes the name and email into the correct format for ThriveCart
  3. The visitor is redirected to your ThriveCart product checkout page
  4. ThriveCart checkout fields for name and email are automatically pre-filled
  5. With Sitewide Identity Persistence on, the Buy links for your product are pre-filled for the rest of their visit too
  6. Customer completes purchase faster

No complex setup, integrations or third-party connectors required.

  • Not affiliated with or provided by Thrive Themes, Kit or ThriveCart. This is a 3rd-party bridging tool. Thrive Themes, Kit and ThriveCart are trademarks of their respective owners. Cart Conversion Boost is an independent product and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Thrive Themes, Kit or ThriveCart.

Key Features

  • Automatically pass name and email to ThriveCart
  • Works with Thrive Themes, Kit (ConvertKit), Elementor, Flodesk, MailerLite, ActiveCampaign, AWeber, GetResponse, BirdSend and any other opt-in form or page builder on your page
  • Handles full name, first name and last name fields
  • Works with ThriveCart hosted, embedded and popup checkouts
  • Lightweight and fast
  • No external dependencies (just your opt-in form and ThriveCart)
  • No tracking or analytics
  • Simple setup
  • No cookies, and nothing is stored on your server
  • GDPR-friendly approach

Use Cases

Cart Conversion Boost is useful for:

Free-plus-shipping offers
Course creators
Digital product sellers
Membership sites
Service providers
Marketing funnels
Lead magnet funnels

Any funnel using a Thrive Themes or Kit opt-in followed by a ThriveCart checkout can benefit.

Requirements

  • WordPress
  • ThriveCart account (Basic or Pro)

Optional:
* Your own page builder and/or form builder – Works with Thrive Themes (Thrive Architect or Thrive Leads), Kit (ConvertKit), Elementor, Flodesk, MailerLite, MailChimp, ActiveCampaign, AWeber, GetResponse, BirdSend, Contact Form 7, ConvertBox, WP Forms, Gravity Forms and any opt-in form builder (excluding iframes).
* You can use the Cart Conversion Boost Pop-up Builder inside the plugin if you don’t have a pop-up builder.

Silent Opt-in

On your sales page, your Buy button should open up an onClick pop-up with the opt-in to start the order “Where should we send your order details to?”, and collect their name and email address.

When Cart Conversion Boost already knows the visitor’s name and email, (from a previous opt-in, or because they clicked an email link carrying their name and email [Note – we will show you how to do this link, if you don’t already know] ) the pop-up is not shown.
Instead, the pop-up form is invisibly filled in and submitted for them. Their details go to your email list (eg cart abandonment follow-up emails) and Cart Conversion Boost redirects them as usual to your ThriveCart checkout. The next thing they see after clicking the Buy button is the pre-filled checkout.

The Buy button pop-up will be shown (pre-filled where possible) if:

  • the visitor is not known yet
  • the pop-up form does not lead to your checkout, or (for Thrive forms) “Send form values” is not ticked
  • the form has a tick box (for example a consent box), a captcha, a drop-down, or a required field that cannot be filled from the visitor’s name and email – the plugin never answers these for a visitor
  • Thrive Themes, Kit or Elementor rejects a value, or the hidden submit has not gone through after 12 seconds

Important: the pop-up form’s Target URL (Thrive), redirect address (Kit) or Redirect (Elementor) must be your Cart Conversion Boost URL, or the cart will not be pre-filled. The “Buy” Button Pop-up does this for you.

Kit pop-up forms that open on a timer, on scroll or on exit are shown as normal, as are Thrive Leads boxes that open on exit. You can switch the feature off on the settings page.

License

This plugin is licensed under the GPLv2 or later.

Additional Notes

If you are using the Pro version of Cart Conversion Boost, please deactivate and delete it before activating this free version to avoid conflicts.

External services

Your visitors’ details never come to us. The only thing that can reach us is your own name and email, when you click one of the plugin’s upgrade links, so the upgrade page is filled in for you (see “Cart Conversion Boost (upgrade page)” below). The services that do receive your visitors’ details are ones you, the site owner, have chosen and set up. This section lists each one, what is sent and when.

ThriveCart (your checkout)

What it is used for: pre-filling the name and email boxes on your ThriveCart checkout.

What is sent and when: when a visitor clicks one of your Buy links, or is sent on from your opt-in form through your Cart Conversion Boost URL, their email address and name (full name, first name and last name, whichever are known) are added to the address of your ThriveCart checkout page. Nothing is sent until the visitor goes to the checkout.

ThriveCart terms: https://legal.thrivecart.com/platform/terms/
ThriveCart privacy policy: https://legal.thrivecart.com/platform/privacy/

Your email provider (through your own opt-in form)

What it is used for: adding a buyer to your own list when they click Buy, without asking them to type their details a second time (Silent opt-in and the “Buy” Button Pop-up).

What is sent and when: only if you switch on Silent opt-in or use the “Buy” Button Pop-up. When a visitor who has already given their name and email on your site clicks your Buy button, the plugin fills in your own opt-in form with those details and submits it for them. Your form then sends the details to whichever email provider you connected it to (for example Kit, MailerLite, Mailchimp, ActiveCampaign, AWeber, BirdSend, Flodesk or GetResponse), exactly as if the visitor had pressed the form’s button. The plugin never ticks a consent box or answers a captcha for a visitor.

Which provider receives the details, and what it does with them, depends on the form you chose. Please see your provider’s own terms and privacy policy.

GetResponse

What it is used for: Silent opt-in when your pop-up holds a GetResponse form. GetResponse forms are sealed off from other scripts, so the plugin cannot press the form’s button. It sends the sign-up to GetResponse itself.

What is sent and when: only if you use a GetResponse form in the “Buy” Button Pop-up with Silent opt-in on, and only for a form that asks for a name and email with no captcha, consent box or other field. When a visitor you already know clicks Buy, the plugin sends their name and email to GetResponse, with the details of your form and list, to add them to your GetResponse list. The plugin also reads your form’s settings from GetResponse. No visitor details are sent with that request.

GetResponse terms: https://www.getresponse.com/legal
GetResponse privacy policy: https://www.getresponse.com/legal/privacy

Kit (ConvertKit)

What it is used for: checking where your Kit form sends people after they subscribe, so Silent opt-in only runs for a form that leads to your checkout.

What is sent and when: only if Silent opt-in is on and the page has one of Kit’s current forms. For a visitor you already know, the plugin reads that form’s settings file from Kit (kit.com). No visitor details and no cookies are sent with that request. If the visitor then clicks Buy, their details reach Kit through your Kit form, as described under “Your email provider” above.

Kit terms: https://kit.com/terms
Kit privacy policy: https://kit.com/privacy

Cart Conversion Boost (upgrade page)

What it is used for: a quicker upgrade to Cart Conversion Boost Pro. When you click an upgrade link in the plugin, the upgrade page and checkout open with your name and email already filled in, so you can pick a plan and pay without typing them.

What is sent and when: only when you click one of the plugin’s upgrade links (“+ Add Another Product”, “get Cart Conversion Boost Pro” or the Pro links on the pop-ups screen), your WordPress first and last name (or your display name, if it is not your email or username) and your account email are added to the upgrade page address. Nothing is sent before you click, nothing is sent in the background, and none of your visitors’ details are ever sent. This is on by default. To keep the links plain, untick “Fill in my name and email when I open the upgrade page” at the bottom of the plugin’s settings page (each admin user chooses for themselves).

Cart Conversion Boost privacy policy: https://cartconversionboost.com/privacy-policy/
sections.installation:
See the installation video at https://cartconversionboost.com/how-to-use-cart-conversion-boost-plugin/

  1. Install via the WordPress plugin repository.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen in WordPress.
  3. Navigate to the Cart Conversion Boost plugin settings page in your admin dashboard.
  4. Add your product’s ThriveCart Checkout URL (see below) and save. Copy your Cart Conversion Boost URL (it looks like yoursite.com/cpccb/0).
  5. Set your opt-in form to send visitors to your Cart Conversion Boost URL after they opt in:

MAKE SURE that form values (name and email) are sent from the opt-in form to the next page.

Thrive Themes: click your opt-in form – “After successful submission” – “Redirect to Custom URL” – paste your Cart Conversion Boost URL as the Target URL, and tick / check “Send form values”.

Kit form (embedded, or the Kit plugin’s Form block): in Kit, open your form – Settings – “After subscribing” – choose “Redirect to an external page” – and paste your Cart Conversion Boost URL.

Kit plugin Form Builder block: set the block’s “Redirect” setting to your Cart Conversion Boost URL.

Elementor Pro form: in the form’s Actions After Submit, add Redirect and paste your Cart Conversion Boost URL. The name and email are added automatically.

Other opt-in forms on your page (Flodesk, BirdSend, MailerLite, Mailchimp, ActiveCampaign, AWeber, GetResponse, Brevo, HubSpot, Contact Form 7, WPForms, Fluent Forms, Gravity Forms, Divi and others): set the form to send people to your Cart Conversion Boost URL after they sign up. Flodesk: in the form’s settings choose On success > Redirect and paste your Cart Conversion Boost URL. BirdSend: install BirdSend’s WordPress plugin and connect it, put the form on your page with its shortcode (for example [birdsend form=123]), and in the form’s Post-Submit choose a redirect and paste your Cart Conversion Boost URL. In the form’s Display Trigger, untick “Don’t show if submitted in the last 30 days”, or people who have already signed up will not see the form. MailerLite: use the JavaScript embed, turn off reCAPTCHA on the form (MailerLite switches it on for new forms) and add a Name field (new MailerLite forms ask for an email only). ActiveCampaign: set On Submit to Open URL with your Cart Conversion Boost URL. AWeber: set the form’s Thank You page to a custom page with your Cart Conversion Boost URL. GetResponse: see “Using GetResponse?” below. The plugin finds the name and email boxes by their labels, so keep labels such as “First name” and “Email”. Forms shown inside an iframe (for example Typeform, Jotform or Google Forms) cannot be read by any plugin on your page, so they are not supported. Mailchimp’s standard embed code opens a new tab – that works too: the name and email are passed across to the new tab. ConvertBox: redirect to your Cart Conversion Boost URL with the form fields passed in the URL as email and name.

3-step funnel (squeeze lead magnet opt-in, then sales page, then checkout):

Send the squeeze page opt-in to your sales page and include form values (Thrive: tick “Send form values”; Kit: redirect to your sales page, or show Kit’s success message on the same page).
When someone clicks on your sales page Buy button, if you want to put them into a separate email list for cart abandonment, different from your squeeze opt-in list (this is wise), then add a pop-up opt-in form to that Buy button (use the Cart Conversion Boost Buy button pop-up, or your own pop-up builder like Thrive or Elementor etc). This opt-in form needs to send to your Cart Conversion Boost URL and include form values.

If you don’t want to set up a separate email list for cart abandonment, and only use the email list from your squeeze opt-in, then this sales page Buy button can either link directly to your ThriveCart product URL or to your Cart Conversion Boost URL. The visitor’s name and email are added automatically, and the ThriveCart checkout gets pre-filled with their name and email.

What to save as your product’s ThriveCart Checkout URL:

The Checkout URL is the address of the page where your buyer pays. It is one of these three:

  • A thrivecart.com product page: your product’s ThriveCart address, for example https://yourname.thrivecart.com/your-product/
  • Your own checkout domain (a subdomain): if your ThriveCart checkout runs on your own domain, the product’s address there, for example https://pay.yourdomain.com/your-product/
  • An embedded checkout: if the ThriveCart cart is embedded on one of your own pages, the address of that page, for example https://yourdomain.com/checkout/

Then use it the same way for all three: save the product, copy its Cart Conversion Boost URL, and use that URL wherever you send the buyer to the cart. An opt-in that sends the buyer to the cart must always use the Cart Conversion Boost URL as its Target URL (Thrive) or redirect address (Kit) or the equivalent name in your form builder. Otherwise the cart will not be pre-filled.

Kit-hosted landing pages (on Kit’s own domain) are not supported, because the plugin can only run on your own WordPress site. Put the Kit form on a page on your site instead.
sections.faq:
How does the “Buy” Button Pop-up work?

Tick “Buy” Button Pop-up on the settings page, then open Cart Conversion Boost – “Buy” Button Pop-ups and add a pop-up: paste your email tool’s embed code (or a form plugin’s shortcode), pick the product it leads to and choose a look. Link any Buy button to the pop-up’s address (#ccb-popup-1), or use the shortcode [ccb_buy_button popup="1" text="Buy Now"] (add style="plain" to use your theme’s button style). After sign-up the buyer always goes to that product’s Cart Conversion Boost URL, pre-filled, so you don’t need to set a redirect in your email tool. The pop-up is only added to pages that link to it, and the form’s code loads after the page, so it never slows your pages down. The free version has one pop-up; Pro has unlimited pop-ups. Thrive, Elementor Pro and Kit modal pop-ups don’t need it: Cart Conversion Boost already works with them.

Does it work with my form builder?

Almost certainly. The plugin reads the name and email boxes of any opt-in form on your page, whichever tool made it: Thrive, Kit, Elementor, Flodesk, BirdSend, MailerLite, Mailchimp, ActiveCampaign, AWeber, GetResponse, EmailOctopus, Brevo, HubSpot, Contact Form 7, WPForms, Fluent Forms, Gravity Forms, Divi, Beaver Builder, Bricks or your own HTML. It finds the boxes by their names, browser hints or the labels your visitors see, and it never touches hidden anti-spam boxes. The exception is a form shown inside an iframe (Typeform, Jotform, Google Forms): no plugin can read those. Silent opt-in (skipping the Buy-button pop-up) works with Thrive Architect, Thrive Leads, Kit and Elementor Pro pop-ups, and with the “Buy” Button Pop-up holding a form from Flodesk, MailerLite, ActiveCampaign, AWeber, GetResponse or another email tool. GetResponse forms work too, but they cannot be pre-filled (see “Using GetResponse?”). EmailOctopus forms have a built-in captcha, so a visitor you already know sees the pop-up with their details filled in and clicks once to go on.

An Elementor form says my submission “seems like spam”. Is that Cart Conversion Boost?

No. That message comes from Akismet, the spam filter that Elementor Pro forms use when the Akismet plugin is active on your site. Cart Conversion Boost never blocks or rejects a form. If real sign-ups are being turned away, open the form in Elementor, go to Content > Akismet Spam Protection, and switch it off for that form (or add another spam check, such as Elementor’s honeypot field).

Using BirdSend?

It works with BirdSend’s in-content forms, on your page or inside the “Buy” Button Pop-up. Install BirdSend’s WordPress plugin and connect it to your BirdSend account, then:

  • Add the form with its shortcode, for example [birdsend form=123] (on your page, or pasted into the pop-up’s “Your opt-in form” box).
  • In BirdSend, open the form – Post-Submit – and redirect to your Cart Conversion Boost URL. BirdSend sometimes asks a visitor to complete a captcha before it saves a sign-up; with the redirect set, the visitor sees the captcha if it appears, then goes on to your pre-filled checkout, and the sign-up is saved.
  • In Form Setup – Display Trigger, untick “Don’t show if submitted in the last 30 days” (it is ticked when you create a form). Otherwise BirdSend hides the form from anyone who signed up in the last 30 days, and your returning buyers, the ones Cart Conversion Boost already knows, see no form on the page.
  • BirdSend forms come with a consent tick box (“We will also send you emails about our products and special offers”). Cart Conversion Boost never ticks a consent box for anyone, so with that box in the form, Silent opt-in shows the pop-up (pre-filled) instead of skipping it, and the visitor ticks it and clicks once. If your sign-up wording and privacy policy mean you don’t need that box, you can remove it from the form in BirdSend, and Silent opt-in then skips the pop-up as usual. Whether you need it depends on where you and your buyers are, so check your own consent rules.

Using MailerLite?

Use MailerLite’s JavaScript embed (the Universal snippet plus the form code), on your page or pasted into the “Buy” Button Pop-up. Turn off reCAPTCHA on the form: MailerLite switches it on for new forms, and with it on, Silent opt-in shows the pop-up instead of skipping it. Add a Name field too: new MailerLite forms ask for an email only. For a form on your page, set its success page to redirect to your Cart Conversion Boost URL; in the pop-up you don’t need a redirect.

Using ActiveCampaign?

In the “Buy” Button Pop-up, leave the form’s On Submit as “Show thank you”: Cart Conversion Boost sees the thank-you message and sends the buyer to the pre-filled checkout. For a form on your page that should go straight to the checkout, set On Submit to “Open URL” with your Cart Conversion Boost URL (for a 3-step funnel squeeze page, your sales page).

Using AWeber?

For a form on your page, set its Thank You page to a custom page with your Cart Conversion Boost URL. In the “Buy” Button Pop-up there is nothing to set: Cart Conversion Boost points AWeber’s thank-you page at your Cart Conversion Boost URL. After a few sign-ups from the same browser AWeber can ask for a captcha before it saves a sign-up; the visitor sees it, completes it and lands on the pre-filled checkout, so the sign-up is saved.

Using GetResponse?

GetResponse’s current forms (“Embedded in a page”, made under Forms and popups) work on your page, in the “Buy” Button Pop-up and with Silent opt-in. Paste both parts of GetResponse’s code: the Web Connect code and the form code. In the pop-up, leave Success view on “Show thank you page”; Cart Conversion Boost sends the buyer to the pre-filled checkout. On your page, set Success view to “Redirect to another page or site” with your Cart Conversion Boost URL (or your sales page, for a 3-step funnel); GetResponse opens it in a new tab and the details carry over. GetResponse seals its forms off from the rest of your page, so they cannot be pre-filled: visitors type their details. Silent opt-in sends the sign-up for a visitor you already know when the form asks only for a name and email, with no captcha or consent box; otherwise the pop-up is shown.

Does this plugin require ThriveCart?

Yes. This plugin is designed specifically to work with ThriveCart checkout pages.

Which opt-in forms does it work with?

Thrive, Kit, Elementor, Flodesk, BirdSend, MailerLite, Mailchimp, ActiveCampaign, AWeber, GetResponse, EmailOctopus, Brevo, HubSpot, Contact Form 7, WPForms, Fluent Forms, Gravity Forms, Divi, Beaver Builder, Bricks or your own HTML.
If you want us to add your opt-in form platform to this plugin, contact us to request it.

What data is passed to ThriveCart?

  • Email address
  • Full name, first name and last name (whichever your opt-in form collects – see “First Name, Last Name and Full Name” section below)

My Kit form only asks for a first name. Will the checkout still work?

Yes. The first name and email are pre-filled. If your ThriveCart checkout also asks for a last name, the buyer types it. To pass the last name too, add a Kit custom field with the key last_name to your form.

Can I use this with the Pro version?

You use this free version OR the Pro version – the Pro version is available at CartConversionBoost.com – One or the other. If the Pro version is active, the free version will automatically deactivate to prevent conflicts. The free version has every feature that the Pro does, just for one product. The Pro version is the same plugin for an unlimited number of products, so you can scale and grow your revenue.

Does this store user data or use cookies?

No cookies are used and no visitor data is stored on your server. The name and email are kept in the visitor’s browser session storage so your checkout can be pre-filled during the same visit. Browser session storage is cleared when the visitor closes the browser tab or window, and the data is never sent to us. It is only passed to your ThriveCart checkout and your own email provider. See the “Privacy, Cookies and Browser Storage” and “External services” sections below for details.

Can I greet visitors by name?

Yes. Once Cart Conversion Boost knows a visitor (they signed up through one of your forms, or arrived from one of your emails with ?tve_name= and email= in the link), [ccb_first_name default="friend"] shows their first name. “Hi [ccb_first_name default="friend"], your checkout is ready” reads “Hi Sam, your checkout is ready” for Sam and “Hi friend, your checkout is ready” for someone new.

In a page builder where shortcodes are awkward (Thrive Architect text, Elementor headings), add the CSS class ccb-first-name to a text element whose text is just the default word.

[ccb_known]...[/ccb_known] shows its content only to visitors the plugin knows, and `[ccb_unknown]...[/ccb_unknown]` only to new visitors. The classes `ccb-known` and `ccb-unknown` do the same on any element or section. Use them to hide a sign-up box from people already on your list, or to show a welcome-back line. Add `tag="span"` to use them inside a sentence.

The name is filled in by the visitor’s own browser from the details the plugin already holds for the visit, so it works on cached pages, adds no cookies and stores nothing new. With Sitewide Identity Persistence on, the greeting follows the visitor to every page of their visit. The default word shows for a moment before the name appears. Copy-and-paste examples are in the “Name greeting” box on the plugin’s settings page.

Does this require coding?

No. Setup is designed to be simple and user-friendly. Just copy and paste your URL as shown in the easy-to-follow instructions.

Disclaimer

Cart Conversion Boost is an independent plugin and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Thrive Themes, Kit or ThriveCart.

First Name, Last Name and Full Name

Opt-in forms and checkouts ask for names in different ways, and Cart Conversion Boost handles each of them:

  • Opt-in asks for a full name (Thrive Themes default): the full name is sent, and also split into first name (the first word) and last name (the rest). “Mary Ann Smith” becomes Mary / Ann Smith, which the buyer can edit if needed.
  • Opt-in asks for a first name only (Kit default): the first name is sent. No last name is guessed – if your checkout asks for one, the buyer types it.
  • Opt-in asks for first name and last name separately: both are sent exactly as entered, with no splitting, and the full name is the two joined together. In Kit, add a custom field with the key last_name. In Thrive, add a field named last_name.
  • Opt-in asks for email only: just the email is sent.

On the ThriveCart side, whether your checkout shows one “full name” box or separate first and last name boxes, the right boxes are filled, because the full name, first name and last name are all sent (whenever they are known).

Privacy, Cookies and Browser Storage

Cart Conversion Boost does not set any cookies, stores nothing on your server, and does not send visitor data to us. We never see, collect or receive your visitors’ names or email addresses. The details only ever go where you have set them to go: your ThriveCart checkout and your own email provider (see “External services” at the end of this readme).

To pre-fill checkouts after a Kit form or another on-page opt-in form, and across pages with Sitewide Identity Persistence, the visitor’s name and email are kept in the browser’s session storage (sessionStorage). This browser session storage:

  • stays in the visitor’s own browser and is never sent to us
  • can only be read by your own website
  • is cleared when the visitor closes the browser tab or window
  • is never used for tracking, analytics or advertising

One exception: when a sign-up form opens a new browser tab (Mailchimp’s standard embed code does this), session storage cannot reach the new tab. For that case only, the name and email are also kept in the browser’s local storage for up to two minutes, and deleted as soon as the new tab has picked them up (or when the two minutes are up).

In URL Mode (Sitewide Identity Persistence off), nothing is kept for Thrive Themes opt-ins (the details travel in the redirect URL), and details from a Kit form or another on-page form are removed from session storage as soon as the checkout link has used them. The Kit plugin’s Form Builder block submits through WordPress, so for that block, the details are passed in the redirect URL, just like Thrive.

With the Silent opt-in, when a visitor you already know clicks your Buy button, the details they have already given are submitted to your own pop-up opt-in form for them, exactly as if they had pressed its button. The form sends them to your email provider as it normally does. The plugin never ticks a consent box or answers a captcha for a visitor: a form with either is always shown.

A note on privacy law: UK and EU rules (PECR and the ePrivacy Directive) cover any storage of information on a visitor’s device, not only cookies. They exempt storage that is strictly necessary to provide a service the visitor has asked for. Cart Conversion Boost only keeps details the visitor has just typed into your opt-in form (or that arrived in a link you sent them), and only uses them to pre-fill your forms and checkout for that visitor during their visit, so we believe this falls within the “strictly necessary” exemption. You remain responsible for your own website’s privacy policy, and we recommend mentioning this pre-fill feature there. This is not legal advice.

The plugin’s upgrade links now open the upgrade page with your name and email already filled in, so there is nothing to type before you choose a plan. Nothing changes in what the plugin does. It makes new tools, and changes in the tools you already use, quicker and safer to support.

short_description: Recover the 70.2% who never buy. Capture every ThriveCart checkout visitor before they disappear and remove the friction of typing their details twice
description:
Cart Conversion Boost helps you increase your checkout conversion rate by first helping you take the name and email before the shopping cart (so you can follow up with the cart abandonment to bring back sales), and then passing the customer’s name and email from your opt-in form into your ThriveCart checkout page *. It works with:

  • Thrive Themes opt-in forms (Thrive Architect and Thrive Leads, including 2-step lightbox opt-ins)
  • Kit (formerly ConvertKit) forms on your WordPress site (Kit’s embedded forms, the Kit plugin’s Form block, and the Kit plugin’s Form Builder block)
  • Elementor Pro forms and popups
  • Any other opt-in form or page builder – Flodesk, BirdSend, MailerLite, Mailchimp, ActiveCampaign, AWeber, GetResponse, Brevo, HubSpot, Contact Form 7, WPForms, Fluent Forms, Gravity Forms, Divi, Beaver Builder, Bricks and hand-written HTML forms – as long as the form sits on your page (not inside an iframe) and sends people to your Cart Conversion Boost URL
  • “Buy” Button Pop-up (new) – no pop-up builder? Cart Conversion Boost has its own. Tick/check it on, paste your email tool’s opt-in form (Flodesk, BirdSend, MailerLite, ActiveCampaign, AWeber, GetResponse, EmailOctopus, Mailchimp, Brevo, a form plugin and others) and link any Buy button to #ccb-popup-1, or use the shortcode [ccb_buy_button popup="1" text="Buy Now"]. Visitors sign up in the pop-up and land on your pre-filled checkout; visitors you already know skip it (Silent opt-in, popup is never seen, but they do go into your cart-abandonment list). Ready-made “Order step” look with an editable headline, step cue and progress bar

Take the customer details before they get to the shopping cart, so you can follow up, and convert more to completed sale, in case of cart abandonment.

When a visitor signs up through your pre-cart opt-in form (as the first part of their order), this plugin ensures their name and email address are automatically pre-filled on the ThriveCart payment page – reducing friction and improving the user experience.

The free version has every feature, for one product:

NOTE: “Known customer” means your site already took their name and email. That might be from a previous opt-in form or from them clicking a link with their name and email address in that link (often from an email you sent them). [We will show you how to set up this email link carrying their name and email, if you don’t already know.]

  • One product – one Cart Conversion Boost URL for one ThriveCart product. Its checkout can be on thrivecart.com, on your own checkout domain (for example pay.yourdomain.com), or embedded on one of your pages
  • Auto-fills your Buy links – on your pages, links to your product’s ThriveCart checkout or to your Cart Conversion Boost URL get the visitor’s details added automatically, so a 3-step funnel (opt-in, sales page, checkout) needs no special links
  • Sitewide Identity Persistence – For known customers, Sitewide Identity Persistence remembers the visitor across every page of your site for the rest of their visit, so the Buy button on any page opens a pre-filled checkout
  • Opt-in pre-fill – For known customers, pre-fill any of your opt-in forms with their name and email, so it’s one click to continue (GetResponse forms are the exception: GetResponse seals them off, so visitors type their details)
  • Silent opt-in – For known customers, when a visitor clicks a Buy button that would normally open a pop-up opt-in, the pop-up is not shown. Instead, its form is invisibly pre-filled in and submitted to your email system behind the scenes, so they still join your list for that form (for example your cart-abandonment list). They never see the popup and the next thing they see is the pre-filled checkout
  • Embedded and popup checkouts – your product’s ThriveCart checkout embedded on your own page is pre-filled too

Cart Conversion Boost Pro is the same plugin, but with unlimited products.

Disclaimer – Cart Conversion Boost is an independent plugin and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Thrive Themes, Kit or ThriveCart.

Video Overview

Watch how Cart Conversion Boost works in under 2 minutes:

Screenshots

  1. The plugin interface screenshot-1.jpg
  2. Paste your Cart Conversion Boost URL into your ThriveThemes optin form as the “Target URL”. Make sure to tick/check the “Send form values” field.
  3. Customer enters their name and email in the pre-sale opt-in
  4. Your ThriveCart checkout is automatically pre-filled with their name and email already, helping conversion to sale. No repeated typing.

🚀 Key Benefits

  • Improve conversion rates – more sales, same traffic
  • Reduced cart abandonment
  • Capture the lead before the payment page
  • Pre-fill ThriveCart checkout fields automatically
  • Reduce friction during checkout – Faster checkout experience
  • Simple setup inside WordPress admin
  • Lightweight and performance-friendly
  • NoCode interface

A smoother checkout experience often leads to higher completion rates and better user experience.

Why This Matters

Every extra step in a checkout process increases the chance that a customer abandons their purchase.

When customers must re-enter information they already provided, it introduces:

Friction
Delay
Drop-off risk

= Less sales.

Cart Conversion Boost removes this friction by connecting your opt-in form and your ThriveCart checkout.

🔗 How It Works

  1. A visitor completes your opt-in form (maybe from a squeeze or lead magnet page, or a pre-cart order pop-up), which captures their name and email and sends them to your email provider
  2. The Cart Conversion Boost plugin passes the name and email into the correct format for ThriveCart
  3. The visitor is redirected to your ThriveCart product checkout page
  4. ThriveCart checkout fields for name and email are automatically pre-filled
  5. With Sitewide Identity Persistence on, the Buy links for your product are pre-filled for the rest of their visit too
  6. Customer completes purchase faster

No complex setup, integrations or third-party connectors required.

  • Not affiliated with or provided by Thrive Themes, Kit or ThriveCart. This is a 3rd-party bridging tool. Thrive Themes, Kit and ThriveCart are trademarks of their respective owners. Cart Conversion Boost is an independent product and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Thrive Themes, Kit or ThriveCart.

Key Features

  • Automatically pass name and email to ThriveCart
  • Works with Thrive Themes, Kit (ConvertKit), Elementor, Flodesk, MailerLite, ActiveCampaign, AWeber, GetResponse, BirdSend and any other opt-in form or page builder on your page
  • Handles full name, first name and last name fields
  • Works with ThriveCart hosted, embedded and popup checkouts
  • Lightweight and fast
  • No external dependencies (just your opt-in form and ThriveCart)
  • No tracking or analytics
  • Simple setup
  • No cookies, and nothing is stored on your server
  • GDPR-friendly approach

Use Cases

Cart Conversion Boost is useful for:

Free-plus-shipping offers
Course creators
Digital product sellers
Membership sites
Service providers
Marketing funnels
Lead magnet funnels

Any funnel using a Thrive Themes or Kit opt-in followed by a ThriveCart checkout can benefit.

Requirements

  • WordPress
  • ThriveCart account (Basic or Pro)

Optional:
* Your own page builder and/or form builder – Works with Thrive Themes (Thrive Architect or Thrive Leads), Kit (ConvertKit), Elementor, Flodesk, MailerLite, MailChimp, ActiveCampaign, AWeber, GetResponse, BirdSend, Contact Form 7, ConvertBox, WP Forms, Gravity Forms and any opt-in form builder (excluding iframes).
* You can use the Cart Conversion Boost Pop-up Builder inside the plugin if you don’t have a pop-up builder.

Silent Opt-in

On your sales page, your Buy button should open up an onClick pop-up with the opt-in to start the order “Where should we send your order details to?”, and collect their name and email address.

When Cart Conversion Boost already knows the visitor’s name and email, (from a previous opt-in, or because they clicked an email link carrying their name and email [Note – we will show you how to do this link, if you don’t already know] ) the pop-up is not shown.
Instead, the pop-up form is invisibly filled in and submitted for them. Their details go to your email list (eg cart abandonment follow-up emails) and Cart Conversion Boost redirects them as usual to your ThriveCart checkout. The next thing they see after clicking the Buy button is the pre-filled checkout.

The Buy button pop-up will be shown (pre-filled where possible) if:

  • the visitor is not known yet
  • the pop-up form does not lead to your checkout, or (for Thrive forms) “Send form values” is not ticked
  • the form has a tick box (for example a consent box), a captcha, a drop-down, or a required field that cannot be filled from the visitor’s name and email – the plugin never answers these for a visitor
  • Thrive Themes, Kit or Elementor rejects a value, or the hidden submit has not gone through after 12 seconds

Important: the pop-up form’s Target URL (Thrive), redirect address (Kit) or Redirect (Elementor) must be your Cart Conversion Boost URL, or the cart will not be pre-filled. The “Buy” Button Pop-up does this for you.

Kit pop-up forms that open on a timer, on scroll or on exit are shown as normal, as are Thrive Leads boxes that open on exit. You can switch the feature off on the settings page.

License

This plugin is licensed under the GPLv2 or later.

Additional Notes

If you are using the Pro version of Cart Conversion Boost, please deactivate and delete it before activating this free version to avoid conflicts.

External services

Your visitors’ details never come to us. The only thing that can reach us is your own name and email, when you click one of the plugin’s upgrade links, so the upgrade page is filled in for you (see “Cart Conversion Boost (upgrade page)” below). The services that do receive your visitors’ details are ones you, the site owner, have chosen and set up. This section lists each one, what is sent and when.

ThriveCart (your checkout)

What it is used for: pre-filling the name and email boxes on your ThriveCart checkout.

What is sent and when: when a visitor clicks one of your Buy links, or is sent on from your opt-in form through your Cart Conversion Boost URL, their email address and name (full name, first name and last name, whichever are known) are added to the address of your ThriveCart checkout page. Nothing is sent until the visitor goes to the checkout.

ThriveCart terms: https://legal.thrivecart.com/platform/terms/
ThriveCart privacy policy: https://legal.thrivecart.com/platform/privacy/

Your email provider (through your own opt-in form)

What it is used for: adding a buyer to your own list when they click Buy, without asking them to type their details a second time (Silent opt-in and the “Buy” Button Pop-up).

What is sent and when: only if you switch on Silent opt-in or use the “Buy” Button Pop-up. When a visitor who has already given their name and email on your site clicks your Buy button, the plugin fills in your own opt-in form with those details and submits it for them. Your form then sends the details to whichever email provider you connected it to (for example Kit, MailerLite, Mailchimp, ActiveCampaign, AWeber, BirdSend, Flodesk or GetResponse), exactly as if the visitor had pressed the form’s button. The plugin never ticks a consent box or answers a captcha for a visitor.

Which provider receives the details, and what it does with them, depends on the form you chose. Please see your provider’s own terms and privacy policy.

GetResponse

What it is used for: Silent opt-in when your pop-up holds a GetResponse form. GetResponse forms are sealed off from other scripts, so the plugin cannot press the form’s button. It sends the sign-up to GetResponse itself.

What is sent and when: only if you use a GetResponse form in the “Buy” Button Pop-up with Silent opt-in on, and only for a form that asks for a name and email with no captcha, consent box or other field. When a visitor you already know clicks Buy, the plugin sends their name and email to GetResponse, with the details of your form and list, to add them to your GetResponse list. The plugin also reads your form’s settings from GetResponse. No visitor details are sent with that request.

GetResponse terms: https://www.getresponse.com/legal
GetResponse privacy policy: https://www.getresponse.com/legal/privacy

Kit (ConvertKit)

What it is used for: checking where your Kit form sends people after they subscribe, so Silent opt-in only runs for a form that leads to your checkout.

What is sent and when: only if Silent opt-in is on and the page has one of Kit’s current forms. For a visitor you already know, the plugin reads that form’s settings file from Kit (kit.com). No visitor details and no cookies are sent with that request. If the visitor then clicks Buy, their details reach Kit through your Kit form, as described under “Your email provider” above.

Kit terms: https://kit.com/terms
Kit privacy policy: https://kit.com/privacy

Cart Conversion Boost (upgrade page)

What it is used for: a quicker upgrade to Cart Conversion Boost Pro. When you click an upgrade link in the plugin, the upgrade page and checkout open with your name and email already filled in, so you can pick a plan and pay without typing them.

What is sent and when: only when you click one of the plugin’s upgrade links (“+ Add Another Product”, “get Cart Conversion Boost Pro” or the Pro links on the pop-ups screen), your WordPress first and last name (or your display name, if it is not your email or username) and your account email are added to the upgrade page address. Nothing is sent before you click, nothing is sent in the background, and none of your visitors’ details are ever sent. This is on by default. To keep the links plain, untick “Fill in my name and email when I open the upgrade page” at the bottom of the plugin’s settings page (each admin user chooses for themselves).

Cart Conversion Boost privacy policy: https://cartconversionboost.com/privacy-policy/
